questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.question: Why does a squirrel-cage induction motor normally run below synchronous speed?

options.text: Slip is required for rotor current to be induced.
The bearings intentionally slow the rotor.
The rotor is mechanically locked below synchronous speed.

hints: Think about how rotor current is produced.
Rotor current requires relative motion between the rotating field and rotor.

answer.short: Slip is required to induce rotor current and therefore produce torque.
answer.model: An induction motor needs relative speed between the rotating field and rotor so rotor current is induced.
answer.explanation: At synchronous speed there is no relative speed, so no induced rotor EMF and no induction torque.
